## Purpose
The auth data layer. It manages accounts (users and admins), sessions, workspaces and their encrypted Mistral keys, roles, memberships, invite and reset links, sign-in protection and the audit log. Every function opens its own session and returns plain dicts. Errors a person can act on are raised as `AuthError(message, status, code)`.

## Responsibilities
- **Validation:**
  - `_email` checks the regex `^[^@\s]{1,64}@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]{2,}$` and at most 254 characters; otherwise 422 "Enter a valid email address.";
  - `_name` collapses whitespace and enforces a limit;
  - `_policy` wraps the password policy and raises 422 with code "password".
- **Audit:**
  - `_audit(db, action, ...)` adds an `AuditEvent` and also clears the principal cache;
  - `audit()` writes standalone events and never raises;
  - `audit_log(limit ≤500, offset, action, actor, target_id, workspace_id)`: the special filter `action="auth"` matches any action ending in one of `AUTH_ACTIONS` (login, logout, logout_all, session_revoke, password_change, password_reset, invite_accept, switch_workspace);
  - `audit_event(id)` returns the full event plus the current actor and target, up to 10 related events by the same actor or on the same target, and the older and newer ids.
- **Roles:**
  - `ensure_system_roles()` creates or refreshes the built-in roles from code. A custom role that already uses a built-in name is renamed "<name> (custom)".
  - `list_roles()` sorts built-in roles in their code order, then custom roles by name, with member counts.
  - `get_role`, `create_role` (at least one permission; the name is unique case-insensitively), `update_role` (built-in roles cannot be changed: 409 "Built-in roles cannot be changed. Duplicate it to make your own.").
  - `delete_role(reassign_to)`. A role with members cannot be deleted without `reassign_to`: 409 "N membership(s) use this role. Choose a role to move them to first."
- **Workspaces:**
  - `workspace_key(ws)` returns the decrypted key, or `MISTRAL_API_KEY` for `key_source=platform`. It returns None when the workspace is disabled or the key is missing, and caches the result for 60 s.
  - `_forget_key` clears that cache and calls `dependencies.forget_workspace_client`.
  - `ensure_default_workspace()`:
    - creates "Default" (or "Default workspace" if the name is taken) with `key_source=platform`;
    - updates its fingerprint and hint when `MISTRAL_API_KEY` changes;
    - calls `scoping.set_default_workspace`;
    - when `APP_WORKSPACE_ID` is set (a per-workspace worker) it only looks the Default workspace up and never creates or corrects it.
  - `list_workspaces`, and `get_workspace`, which includes `data: count_rows`.
  - `_check_new_key` rejects a key with:
    - 422 "Enter the workspace's Mistral API key." when it is empty;
    - 409 "This key is already used by the workspace “X”." when it is already used;
    - 409 when it is the platform key;
    - 422 or 503 when `verify` fails.
  - `check_key` verifies without saving (the "Test key" button).
  - `create_workspace` stores the key encrypted at version 1 with status valid.
  - `update_workspace` (name, description, disabled). The Default workspace cannot be disabled.
  - `recheck_key`.
  - `mark_key_invalid`, called when Mistral answers 401 mid-request.
  - `rotate_key(ws, api_key, allow_other_workspace)`:
    - the Default workspace's key is changed on the Settings page instead;
    - when `same_workspace` is False and the change is not confirmed: 409 with code `other_workspace`, explaining that existing agents, libraries and conversations would become unreachable;
    - otherwise it bumps `key_version`, re-encrypts, and sets the status to valid and the `rotated_at` time.
  - `delete_workspace`:
    - the Default workspace cannot be deleted;
    - a workspace with members gives 409 "N user(s) still belong…";
    - a workspace that owns data gives 409, listing the counts, with "Disable it instead, so nothing is lost.";
    - deleting also revokes that workspace's sessions.
  - `workspace_members`.
- **Users:**
  - `list_users(q, workspace_id, status, include_deleted)`, and `get_user`, which adds active_sessions, pending_link and password_changed_at.
  - `create_user(email, name, memberships)` creates the user with status invited, the memberships and an invite token, and returns `link`.
  - `update_user`, `set_memberships` (moves `last_workspace_id` when the user leaves that workspace), `issue_link` (an invite while invited or with no password, otherwise a reset; not allowed while disabled), `set_user_status` (disabling revokes sessions; enabling clears the lockout), `unlock_user` and `revoke_user_sessions`.
  - `delete_user`. A user who never signed in is deleted outright. Anyone else is anonymised: status deleted, email `deleted-<id>@deleted.invalid`, name "Deleted user", password cleared, and memberships, tokens and sessions removed.
- **Admins:**
  - `ensure_bootstrap_admin()` runs only when no admin exists. It uses the environment's email and password, validates the policy, and creates an active admin with `must_change_password=True`. Without the environment variables it logs how to create one.
  - `create_admin_with_password` is used by the CLI and resets an existing admin.
  - `list_admins`, and `create_admin`, which sends an invite link.
  - `update_admin`. An admin cannot disable their own account, and the last active admin cannot be disabled.
  - `admin_link`.
  - `delete_admin`, with the same self and last-admin guards.
- **Sign-in:**
  - **IP rate limit.** Only failed attempts count: a deque per IP over 300 s, with a limit of `AUTH_IP_ATTEMPTS`. The map is bounded at 10,000 IPs, dropping 5,000 when it overflows.
  - **`login(kind, email, password, ip, ua)`:**
    1. A rate-limited IP gives 429.
    2. An unknown or deleted account verifies the dummy hash and gives 401 with the generic message "The email or password is incorrect."
    3. A locked account gives 423.
    4. A wrong password increments `failed_logins`. At `max_failed_logins` it sets `locked_until = now + lockout` and resets the counter. The response is 401 with the generic message.
    5. A disabled account gives 403; an invited one gives 403 "Finish setting up your account from your invite link first."
    6. For users it picks a workspace: the preferred one, else `last_workspace_id`, else the first by name among enabled memberships. With none: 403 `no_workspace`.
    7. On success it rehashes the password when needed, resets the counters and creates a session.
    8. Returns `{token, must_change_password}`.
  - **`_create_session`** creates a random token whose sha256 is the session id, with a 16-character `public_id` and `expires_at = now + max hours`.
- **Session resolution:**
  - `resolve_session(kind, token)`:
    - uses a 10 s principal cache, cleared when it passes 20,000 entries;
    - a session that is revoked, expired or idle longer than the idle limit gives None, and expired or idle ones are revoked;
    - builds the principal with `_principal_for`, which re-picks the workspace when the current membership or workspace is gone or disabled;
    - updates `last_seen_at` at most once every 60 s.
  - `logout`, `logout_everywhere(keep_current)`, `list_sessions`, `revoke_session(public_id)`, `switch_workspace` and `my_workspaces`.
  - `change_password`:
    - verifies the current password (403 if it is wrong);
    - the new password must differ from the old one;
    - applies the policy;
    - clears `must_change_password`;
    - revokes the other sessions.
  - `update_profile`.
- **Invite and reset links:**
  - `_token_row`. A used or unknown link gives 410 `link_invalid`; an expired one gives 410 `link_expired`.
  - `link_info`, and `accept_link(token, password, name)`, which sets the password, activates the account, marks the token used, revokes old sessions, picks a workspace and opens a session.
  - `_issue_token` voids previous unused tokens of the same kind for the subject. Invites expire after `invite_days` and resets after `reset_hours`.
  - `_link` builds the path `/invite/<token>` or `/reset-password/<token>`.
- **Admin dashboard and housekeeping:**
  - `overview()` returns user counts by status, workspaces with key problems, role and admin counts, active sessions, and 24-hour sign-in and failure counts.
  - `purge_expired(days=30)` drops sessions and tokens that ended more than 30 days ago.

## Key elements
See Responsibilities.

## Control flow
Each function opens `with _db() as db:`, validates, mutates, writes an audit event and commits. `_db` raises 503 "The database is unavailable." when `SessionLocal` is None.

## Data, state and side effects
- Reads and writes every `auth_*` table.
- In-process caches: `_principals` (10 s), `_key_cache` (60 s) and `_ip_attempts`.

## Configuration
All of `auth/config.py`, plus `MISTRAL_API_KEY` and `APP_WORKSPACE_ID`.

## Interactions
- Used by `routes/auth.py` (sign-in, sessions, links), `routes/admin.py` (the console), `auth/middleware.py`, `dependencies.py`, `health.py` and `auth/cli.py`.

## Error handling and edge cases
- `AuthError` codes include: invalid, email, password, duplicate, not_found, system_role, permissions, in_use, reassign, default, duplicate_key, key_*, other_workspace, has_data, memberships, disabled, self, last_admin, rate_limited, credentials, locked, invited, no_workspace, session, current_password, link_invalid, link_expired, not_member, unavailable.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **Every audit write clears the principal cache**, so a sign-out, disable or role change takes effect on the very next request despite the 10 s cache.
- **The generic credential error and the dummy-hash verification** prevent account enumeration.
- **Only failed sign-ins count toward the IP limit**, so a whole office behind one NAT address can still sign in.
- **Datetimes are naive UTC**: `_now()` strips the tzinfo, and ISO strings get a "Z" suffix.

## How to rebuild this file
Implement the sections in this order: helpers, audit, roles, workspaces, users, admins, sign-in, sessions, links, overview and purge. Use exactly the status codes, error codes and messages above, because the UI shows them.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_auth.py` covers sign-in, lockout, links, workspaces, keys (patched), roles, memberships and deletion.
